prompt.context: Our client is a major Italian conglomerate that owns a movie theatre chain with several theatres in Rome and Milan. The CEO is planning to expand the chain in Florence and has found an interesting theatre in the center of Florence that would sell its activity for €2M. 'Cinema Firenze' has only one room that holds 400 seats and is open 50 weeks per year, running 4 shows on weekdays and 5 shows on weekends.
prompt.question: The CEO hired Bain & Co. to understand if they should go through with the acquisition. Should the client acquire Cinema Firenze for €2M?

clarifying_info.q: Why does the client want to buy this theatre?
clarifying_info.a: There are important aspects such as brand image and geographic expansion, but for now focus on the profitability analysis.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average ticket price?

clarifying_info.a: You should estimate it; the most successful theatre in Rome ('L'Adriano') has 30% utilization over the year for reference.
8 employees at average annual salary of €50,000; operating expenses €125,000; film fee 50% of ticket sales; rent €40/m2 per month for 1,000 m2 total area.

clarifying_info.q: What is the margin on concessions?

framework: Define the decision: acquisition at €2M — evaluate profitability and return
Revenue analysis: ticket sales, advertising, concessions
Cost analysis: personnel, operating expenses, film fees, rent
Valuation sanity check: required return vs. actual profit
Synergies and levers if CEO still wants to proceed

questions.prompt: Estimate annual revenues from ticket sales.
questions.guidance: Break capacity into weekday and weekend segments. Calculate weighted average utilization, then derive total tickets sold, then multiply by ticket price.

math.setup: Shows per day × days per week × weeks per year × capacity × utilization = tickets sold; then × price
steps: Annual tickets = 30 shows/week × 50 weeks × 100 tickets = 150,000 tickets

questions.guidance: Assume advertising revenue is proportional to ticket volume. A reasonable assumption is a per-ticket advertising rate.

math.setup: Advertising revenue = tickets sold × advertising rate per ticket

questions.guidance: Estimate the share of customers who buy concessions, the average spend, and the margin. Note that only the net margin flows to profit.

math.setup: Concession revenue = customers × attach rate × spend per customer; net = revenue × margin

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenues and total costs, then derive profit before and after tax.
questions.guidance: Sum all revenue streams; then calculate each cost line using the given data. Apply 40% tax rate to get net income.

math.setup: Total revenue = ticket + advertising + concessions net; Total cost = personnel + opex + film fees + rent; Profit = Revenue − Cost; Net income = Profit × (1−tax)
math.answer: Net income ≈ €79,200 per year; profit margin ≈ 4.5%

questions.prompt: Based on your financial analysis, is this a good acquisition at €2M?
questions.guidance: Compare annual net profit to the acquisition price. Use a simple payback or required-return test. A 10% cost of capital implies needing €200K/year; actual is €79K. Payback period is ~25 years. Clearly unattractive. Also note the 4.5% profit margin is low.

math.setup: Required annual cash flow at 10% cost of capital = acquisition price × 10%; compare to actual
math.answer: Not a good acquisition at €2M. Required return of €200K/year far exceeds the €79K actual. Payback is ~25 years.

brainstorming.prompt: If the CEO insists on acquiring the theatre, how would you make the business more profitable?

categories.name: Revenue — Volume
ideas: Partnerships with local shops for cross-promotion in exchange for visibility
Show films suited to local Florence clientele to drive occupancy
Dynamic/lower pricing for off-peak slots to fill seats
Loyalty programs or group discount deals

categories.name: Revenue — Price
ideas: Premium pricing for peak weekend shows
Add more concession SKUs or upsell combos

categories.name: Cost — Bargaining Power
ideas: Leverage chain status to negotiate lower film fees with distributors (single-theatre vs. chain negotiation)
Consolidate supplier contracts across all theatres in the conglomerate

categories.name: Cost — Operations
ideas: Reduce operating expenses through shared services with other theatres in the chain

categories.name: Synergies
ideas: Geographic expansion brand value — Florence completes Rome/Milan triangle
Cross-promote films and events across theatres
Shared marketing spend across the chain

recommendation: Do not acquire Cinema Firenze at €2M; the net income of ~€79K per year implies a ~25-year payback and a 4.5% profit margin, which is well below the minimum return threshold at a 10% cost of capital.
If the CEO insists on proceeding, negotiate aggressively on price and identify synergies — particularly leveraging the chain's bargaining power to reduce the 50% film fee.
risks: Stagnant or declining cinema attendance in Florence
High fixed costs (especially rent at €480K/year) leave little room for downside
Overpaying at €2M with no clear path to margin improvement
next_steps: Benchmark margin and utilization against other theatres in the client's portfolio
Negotiate acquisition price down substantially (target: price that yields ≤10-year payback)
Quantify potential film-fee savings from chain-level distributor negotiation
Assess whether additional screens or expanded concession offerings could materially lift profitability
